verses.1:1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace.
verses.1:2: We always give thanks to God for all of you, making mention of you in our prayers, constantly
verses.1:3: remembering your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ before our God and Father,
verses.1:4: knowing, brothers loved by God, your election,
verses.1:5: because our gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with great conviction, just as you know what kind of people we proved to be among you for your sake.
verses.1:6: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction with the joy of the Holy Spirit,
verses.1:7: so that you became examples to all who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.
verses.1:8: For from you the word of the Lord has rung out, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place your faith toward God has gone out, so that we have no need to say anything.
verses.1:9: For they themselves report about us what kind of entrance we had to you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve a living and true God,
verses.1:10: and to wait for His Son from the heavens, whom He raised from the dead—Jesus, who rescues us from the wrath that is coming.
verses.2:1: For you yourselves know, brothers, that our entrance to you has not been in vain,
verses.2:2: but having previously suffered and been abusively treated, as you know, in Philippi, we became bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much struggle.
verses.2:3: For our exhortation is not from error, nor from impurity, nor in deceit;
verses.2:4: but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not as pleasing people, but God, who examines our hearts.
verses.2:5: For we never came with a word of flattery, as you know, nor with a pretext for greed—God is witness—
verses.2:6: nor seeking glory from people, neither from you nor from others,
verses.2:7: even though we could have been a burden as apostles of Christ. Yet we became infants among you. Just as a nursing mother cherishes her own children,
verses.2:8: so, longing deeply for you, we were pleased to share with you not only the gospel of God, but also our own lives, because you had become dear to us.
verses.2:9: For you remember, brothers, our labor and hardship: working night and day so as not to burden any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
verses.2:10: You are witnesses, and so is God, how devoutly and righteously and blamelessly we conducted ourselves toward you who believe,
verses.2:11: just as you know how we dealt with each one of you, as a father with his own children,
verses.2:12: exhorting, encouraging, and charging you to walk worthily of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory.
verses.2:13: And for this reason we also give thanks to God constantly, that when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you welcomed it not as the word of people, but as what it truly is, the word of God, which is also at work in you who believe.
verses.2:14: For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God that are in Judea in Christ Jesus, because you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen just as they did from the Jews,
verses.2:15: who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out, and do not please God, and are opposed to all people,
verses.2:16: hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they may be saved, so as always to fill up their sins. But the wrath has come upon them completely.
verses.2:17: Now we, brothers, having been bereaved of you for a brief time, in presence, not in heart, were all the more eager to see your face with great desire.
verses.2:18: For we wanted to come to you—I, Paul, both once and twice—yet Satan blocked us.
verses.2:19: For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting—is it not indeed you—before our Lord Jesus at His coming?
verses.2:20: For you are our glory and joy.
verses.3:1: Therefore, when we could bear it no longer, we were willing to be left behind in Athens alone,
verses.3:2: and we sent Timothy, our brother and servant of God in the gospel of Christ, to establish you and to encourage you concerning your faith,
verses.3:3: so that no one would be unsettled by these afflictions. For you yourselves know that we are destined for this.
verses.3:4: For indeed, when we were with you, we kept telling you in advance that we were going to suffer affliction, just as it also happened, and you know.
verses.3:5: For this reason, when I too could bear it no longer, I sent to learn about your faith, for fear that somehow the tempter had tempted you and our labor would be in vain.
verses.3:6: But now that Timothy has come to us from you and brought us good news of your faith and love, and that you always have a good remembrance of us, longing to see us just as we also long to see you,
verses.3:7: for this reason we were encouraged, brothers, about you in all our distress and affliction through your faith,
verses.3:8: because now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.
verses.3:9: For what thanksgiving can we return to God for you over all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God,
verses.3:10: night and day praying most earnestly to see your face and to complete what is lacking in your faith?
verses.3:11: Now may our God and Father Himself and our Lord Jesus direct our way to you.
verses.3:12: And may the Lord make you increase and overflow in love toward one another and toward all, just as we also do toward you,
verses.3:13: so that He may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His holy ones.
verses.4:1: Finally then, brothers, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus that, just as you received from us how you must walk and please God—just as you also are walking—you would abound even more.
verses.4:2: For you know what commands we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
verses.4:3: For this is God's will, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality,
verses.4:4: that each one of you know how to acquire his own vessel in sanctification and honor,
verses.4:5: not in the passion of desire, even as the Gentiles who do not know God,
verses.4:6: and not to overstep and take advantage of his brother in this matter, because the Lord is an avenger concerning all these things, just as we also told you beforehand and solemnly testified.
verses.4:7: For God did not call us to impurity, but in sanctification.
verses.4:8: Consequently, the one who rejects this does not reject man, but God, who also gives His Holy Spirit to you.
verses.4:9: Now regarding brotherly love, you have no need for anyone to write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another;
verses.4:10: for indeed you are doing this toward all the brothers who are throughout all Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to abound even more,
verses.4:11: and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own affairs, and to work with your own hands, just as we commanded you,
verses.4:12: so that you may walk properly toward those outside and have need of nothing.
verses.4:13: Now we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, concerning those who are asleep, so that you may not grieve as the rest also do who have no hope.
verses.4:14: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose, in the same way God will also bring with Him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus.
verses.4:15: For this we tell you by a word of the Lord, that we who are living, who remain until the coming of the Lord, will by no means precede those who have fallen asleep.
verses.4:16: For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a commanding shout, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first;
verses.4:17: then we who are living, who remain, will be caught up together with them in clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and thus we will always be with the Lord.
verses.4:18: So then, encourage one another with these words.
verses.5:1: Now regarding the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anything to be written to you,
verses.5:2: for you yourselves know thoroughly that the day of the Lord comes just like a thief in the night.
verses.5:3: Whenever they say, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction comes upon them just like birth pains upon a pregnant woman, and they will by no means escape.
verses.5:4: But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief;
verses.5:5: for all of you are sons of light and sons of day; we are neither of night nor of darkness.
verses.5:6: So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us stay awake and be sober.
verses.5:7: For those who sleep, sleep by night, and those who get drunk are drunk by night.
verses.5:8: But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on a breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation.
verses.5:9: For God did not appoint us to wrath, but to the obtaining of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.5:10: who died on our behalf, so that whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.
verses.5:11: Therefore, encourage one another and build each other up, just as indeed you are doing.
verses.5:12: Now we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who labor among you and preside over you in the Lord and admonish you,
verses.5:13: and to regard them most highly in love on account of their work. Live at peace among yourselves.
verses.5:14: And we urge you, brothers: admonish the disorderly, comfort the fainthearted, support the weak, be patient toward all.
verses.5:15: See to it that no one returns evil for evil to anyone, but always pursue what is good, both toward one another and toward all.
verses.5:18: in everything give thanks; for this is God's will in Christ Jesus for you.
verses.5:20: do not treat prophecies with contempt;
verses.5:21: but test all things; hold fast to what is good,
verses.5:22: abstain from every kind of evil.
verses.5:23: Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you thoroughly, and may your spirit and soul and body be preserved whole and blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.5:24: Faithful is the One who calls you, who will also do it.
verses.5:26: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
verses.5:27: I put you under oath by the Lord that this letter be read to all the brothers.
verses.5:28: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

notes.1:2: The adverb "constantly" (ἀδιαλείπτως) stands between verses 2 and 3 and may modify either "making mention" in verse 2 or "remembering" in verse 3.
notes.1:7: Following the earliest manuscripts, the text reads the plural "examples" (τύπους); other manuscripts read the singular "example" (τύπον).
notes.2:7: The phrase "been a burden" (ἐν βάρει εἶναι) can mean either imposing a financial burden (cf. 2:9) or asserting apostolic weight and authority. The earliest manuscripts read "infants" (νήπιοι), whereas other manuscripts read "gentle" (ἤπιοι), a difference of one Greek letter.
notes.2:13: The relative pronoun "which" (ὅς) agrees grammatically with "the word" (λόγον), though some understand it as referring to "God" ("who is also at work").
notes.2:16: The phrase "completely" (εἰς τέλος) is variously understood as "completely / to the utmost," "at last," or "forever."
notes.2:19: "Coming" translates παρουσία, a term used in the ancient world for the official arrival or visit of a ruler and applied in the New Testament to Christ's return.
notes.3:2: The text reads "servant of God" (διάκονον τοῦ θεοῦ); other manuscripts read "coworker of God" (συνεργὸν τοῦ θεοῦ) or combine both titles.
notes.3:3: "Unsettled" translates the rare Greek verb σαίνεσθαι, which originally meant "to fawn" or "wag the tail" and in later Greek came to mean "to be disturbed or shaken."
notes.3:11: The optative verb "direct" (κατευθύναι) is grammatically singular despite its compound subject, "our God and Father Himself and our Lord Jesus."
notes.3:13: "His holy ones" (τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ), echoing Zechariah 14:5, may refer to angels, to believers, or to both together.
notes.4:4: Greek skeuos ("vessel") is widely debated as referring either to one's own body (with ktasthai meaning "possess" or "control") or to one's own wife (with ktasthai meaning "acquire" in marriage).
notes.4:14: The prepositional phrase "through Jesus" (dia tou Iesou) may modify "those who have fallen asleep" (dying in union with Jesus) or the verb "will bring" (God will bring them through Jesus' agency).
notes.4:17: "To meet" translates Greek eis apantesin, a term commonly used in the Greco-Roman world for citizens going out to welcome an approaching dignitary and escort him back into the city.
notes.5:4: The Greek text reads the nominative kleptes ("like a thief"), matching v. 2; some manuscripts read the accusative plural kleptas ("like thieves").
notes.5:10: Here "awake" and "asleep" shift from their moral sense in vv. 6-7 to serve as metaphors for being alive or dead at Christ's return.
notes.5:14: Greek ataktous ("the disorderly") originally denoted soldiers out of rank and here describes members disrupting the community, particularly those refusing to work (cf. 4:11; 2 Thess. 3:6-11).
notes.5:22: Greek eidos ("kind" or "form") may denote either a category/species ("every kind of evil") or a visible appearance ("every appearance of evil").
